facts.statement: The genus Shenqiornis was named and described in 2010 by a team including Wang Xuri, Jingmai O'Connor, and Luis María Chiappe.
facts.quote: The type species Shenqiornis mengi was in 2010 named and described by Wang Xuri, Jingmai O'Connor, Zhao Bo, Luis María Chiappe, Gao Chunling and Cheng Xiaodong.

facts.statement: Shenqiornis fossils were found in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China, where their exact age is uncertain.
facts.quote: It was found in the Qiaotou Member of the Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province, China, and is therefore of uncertain age.

facts.statement: Based on correlations with the Yixian Formation, Shenqiornis is probably dated to the Aptian stage, around 122 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Qiaotou Member may correlate with the more well-known Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation, and so probably is dated to the Aptian, around 122 million years ago.

facts.statement: Shenqiornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Shenqiornis is a genus of enantiornithean dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Shenqiornis belongs to the family Bohaiornithidae.
The discovered specimen has a relatively well-preserved diapsid skull that is somewhat similar to that of Confuciusornis.
facts.quote: El espécimen encontrado tiene un cráneo relativamente bien conservado, del tipo diápsido, similar en cierta medida al de Confuciusornis.

facts.statement: The dentition of Shenqiornis is unique among Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Su dentadura es única entre los Enantiornithes.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a largely complete skeleton of a subadult individual.
rejected.quote: The holotype is DNHM D2950-2951, a plate and counterplate containing a largely complete skeleton of a subadult.
